title: The Mongol Mail That Never Stopped
topic: How the Mongol Yam relay carried messages 200 miles a day
mechanism: No horse ran far: stations every 25 miles kept horses saddled, and riders' bells warned the next station so the letter changed hands at a gallop without ever stopping.

beats.hook: A courier gallops across the dawn steppe; Polo's claim of 200 miles a day, yet no single horse made the trip
beats.but: A horse at full gallop tires long before sunset (the exhausted horse folds under its rider)
beats.then: The Khan builds a Yam station every 25 miles, up to 400 horses, half saddled, half at grass; Polo's 10,000 stations and 300,000 horses on a clerk's tally boards
beats.conflict: The villages next door must supply the horses: a woman with three goats is outraged; the paiza lets a rider take anyone's horse
beats.pivot: You see, no horse ran far, only the letter did: the bells ring out at night long before the rider arrives
beats.so: The next station saddles a fresh horse, the clerk logs the time, the letter changes hands at a gallop; fruit picked in the capital reaches the Khan the next evening
beats.closing: Every horse got tired. The letter never did.

seed.what: The courier's belt of brass bells (and his bound chest), close on it in the hook
